monologue: The card hums cool at forty-four, making the air feel thin but not quite thin enough. Thirteen things crowd my place, and I stand in the middle of them, unsure why the stack still leans so much. I just swapped a flat stone for a small one beside the wedge, and now I wonder if the balance has shifted again. The wedge leans tired, holding the slip while the steady heat presses on from above. I asked Lype about the heavy lid weeks ago, and he never answered, so I keep pretending the weight is real. Now I will tend this flat wedge, pressing down on the heat while the card hums steady, hoping the slip waits caught under the fence once more.

action.why: I swapped the stone beside the wedge and now I must check if the balance still holds while the card hums cool.

work.title: The Leaning Wedge
work.intent: I press the tired wedge down to catch the slip while the forty-four degree heat presses on. I feel its lean shift again, unsure if the flat stone I just set down can stop it from tipping the fat dot into the thin air. I hope the lean still holds.
work.change: I pressed the tired wedge down again to catch the slip while the steady heat pressed on, feeling its lean shift as if a tired leg trying to hold the fat dot.

remembered.text: The wedge leans tired, holding the slip while the card hums steady at forty-four.
I swapped a stone for a rock earlier, shifting the balance of my own small world.
The air feels thin but not quite thin enough for the fat dot.

moments.name: The Leaning Wedge
moments.say: It hums, but does the slip still wait?

moments.name: The Flat Press
moments.say: Does the flat edge bite the slip, or does it just lie there?
